title: Dark clouds and a starry night sky
caption: The center of the Milky Way between the NTT and the ESO 3.6-meter telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The center of the Milky Way rises between two telescopes at ESO's La Silla Observatory, its light splattered among dark clouds. Between the buildings glow two nebulae in the constellation Sagittarius, the Trifid Nebula on the left and the Lagoon Nebula on the right.

Both look red because young stars inside them ionize hydrogen atoms, making the gas glow. The Trifid also carries a blue tint, from dust reflecting some of that starlight. Most of the dust here, though, shows up as dark clouds. Without nearby stars to light it, interstellar dust blocks whatever lies behind and appears black against the stars.

On the left stands the New Technology Telescope (NTT), a pioneer of active optics, which keeps a telescope mirror in shape during observations despite distortions caused by its weight or by temperature. On the right is the ESO 3.6-meter telescope, home to the exoplanet-hunting instruments HARPS and NIRPS.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by José Rodrigues. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The red and blue tints of these nebulae are faint, and a camera gathering light over time may show them far more clearly than the eye.

explore: That second telescope means a great deal to the photographer, José Rodrigues. He grew up with a poster of it on his bedroom wall, dreaming of one day using it to find exoplanets, and he has since realized that dream as an exoplanet researcher.
alt: The bright center of the Milky Way between two telescope buildings, with two small red nebulae between them and dark dust clouds across the band.
